caption: What if you dug a hole straight through the Earth from India? The deepest hole ever drilled, Russia's Kola Superdeep Borehole, reached 12,262 m in 1989 after 19 years of work. Earth is about 12,742 km across, so that's roughly 0.1% of the way. Now imagine a heat-proof tunnel and you jump in. Gravity pulls you faster until you pass the centre at over 8 km per second, more than 28,000 km/h. The inner core is about 5,200°C, close to the Sun's surface at about 5,500°C. Then gravity slows you down, and a 2015 physics study put the whole trip at about 38 minutes. The catch: the point directly opposite India is in the Pacific Ocean, off South America. Splash. Would YOU jump in? 👇
